groups.name: Medicines liable to depress bone marrow function

src.q: Most serious adverse reactions of methotrexate include bone marrow suppression
Tegretol should also be discontinued if any evidence of significant bone marrow depression appears.

conditions.name: Perforated eardrum (known or suspected), or eardrum not intact
Mitochondrial DNA variant (e.g. m.1555A>G) or maternal history of deafness / mitochondrial mutation (aminoglycoside deafness risk)
Previous myelosuppression (bone marrow depression) with chloramphenicol
Family history of blood dyscrasia (e.g. aplastic anaemia)
Viral infection of the cornea or conjunctiva (e.g. vaccinia, varicella)
Disease causing thinning of the cornea or sclera

notes: BATCH AK (eye and ear products). Routes are 'eye' and 'ear'. These local products were NOT added to any systemic group (aminoglycoside, corticosteroid, fluoroquinolone, etc.), so systemic class rules do not fire on them; their own rules point at systemic groups/medicines instead (group:aminoglycoside, group:ototoxic, group:nephrotoxic, group:cephalosporin, group:cyp3a4-inhibitor, group:antidiabetic, furosemide). Note the groups aminoglycoside, ototoxic and nephrotoxic currently have no master-list members, so those rules are inert until another batch sources members. NEW GROUP bone-marrow-depressant (used by the chloramphenicol eye 'drugs liable to depress bone marrow function' rule): members limited to methotrexate and carbamazepine, quoted from their own SmPCs (sources defined in batches F and Q); many other master medicines list rare blood dyscrasias as adverse effects (e.g. co-trimoxazole, mirtazapine, ACE inhibitors) and were deliberately NOT added - the integrator may widen this. USED (3): gentamicin-drops (emc-4218, emc-6552; split into eye-use and ear-use formulations of the same eye/ear drops so the perforated-eardrum rule fires only for ear use; the clinic's gentamicin 0.3% EYE OINTMENT has no UK SmPC on emc or MHRA Products - formulation note says the drops SmPCs are used for eye content), chloramphenicol-eye (ointment emc-9770, emc-7299 - both pharmacy-sale, licensed 2 years and over; drops emc-427 prescription-only all ages, emc-9662/emc-13182 pharmacy-sale 2 years and over, emc-5195 pharmacy-sale adults and children), neomycin-polymyxin-dexamethasone-eye (emc-841 drops, emc-842 ointment). NO UK PRODUCT (4, no rules, every section not-available): neomycin-polymyxin-prednisolone-ear (clinic link emc-2474 is neomycin/polymyxin B/HYDROCORTISONE ear drops - different steroid, not used); gentamicin-dexamethasone-ear (no UK product; DATA MISMATCH: the clinic row gives a trade name/link that is the UK neomycin/polymyxin B/hydrocortisone ear drops, emc-2474 - the clinic entry should be checked); ciprofloxacin-hydrocortisone-ear (UK has ciprofloxacin alone, ciprofloxacin/fluocinolone and ciprofloxacin/dexamethasone ear drops only; clinic link emc-8847 is ciprofloxacin alone); phenol-glycerol-ear (no UK product; MHRA Products has phenol only as oily injection). If the integrator prefers ingredient-level proxies for these ear products, emc-2474 (neomycin/polymyxin B/hydrocortisone: perforated eardrum, aminoglycoside cross-sensitivity, untreated viral/fungal/tubercular infection, not recommended under 3 years, pregnancy/lactation not recommended) is the closest UK label; it was not used to keep to the same-active-ingredient rule. CONFLICTS BETWEEN UK SOURCES: (1) chloramphenicol pregnancy - SmPCs 'not recommended'/'should not be used' (one ointment SmPC: 'use only when considered essential') vs BUMPS 'can be used in pregnancy' and first choice for eye infection; rule level avoid with both in action. (2) chloramphenicol breastfeeding - SmPCs avoid/not recommended vs SPS 'can be used with caution' with infant monitoring; rule level avoid with both. (3) chloramphenicol contraindications differ between SmPCs: personal history of blood dyscrasia is in 4.3 of emc-9770/427/9662/13182 but not emc-7299/5195 (family history only); prior chloramphenicol myelosuppression is not in emc-13182. (4) chloramphenicol under 2 years: pharmacy-sale SmPCs licensed from 2 years vs prescription-only drops (all children) and MHRA DSU 2021 (borax-buffered drops can be safely given aged 0 to 2). (5) neomycin/polymyxin/dexamethasone eye: SmPC pregnancy 'not recommended' vs BUMPS general 'most eye drops can be used'; breastfeeding SmPC 'decide' vs SPS 'can be used'. (6) gentamicin interactions in 4.5 (furosemide ototoxicity, cephalosporin nephrotoxicity, 'avoid unless essential') are carried over from systemic gentamicin; the same SmPC says topical absorption is unlikely to carry a comparable risk - kept at level avoid (source strength) with that context in the consequence. AGE BOUNDS SET BY US: chloramphenicol newborn dose rule uses maxYears 0.08 (about 4 weeks; SmPC says 'new born infants'); eye-steroid child IOP rule uses maxYears 18 (SmPC says 'paediatric patients'). Both stated in the rule consequence. NOT ADDED AS RULES: pharmacy referral criteria for chloramphenicol (glaucoma, dry eye syndrome, recent eye surgery, etc.) are in cautions only; topical NSAID + eye steroid (no ophthalmic NSAID in master list); curare-type muscle relaxants. NOT FOUND: no BUMPS leaflet specific to eye chloramphenicol beyond the general chloramphenicol leaflet; no SPS breastfeeding page for gentamicin or neomycin (SPS chloramphenicol page used for 'gentamicin preferred'); no SPS monitoring pages; NICE CKS geo-blocked, not used. BRAND PRESCRIBING: none stated by any UK source. AUDIT 2026-10-17 (second check, see audit/AJ-AK-AL.md): gentamicin-drops interaction rules (furosemide, ototoxic, cephalosporin, nephrotoxic) kept at avoid (SmPC strength) but concern/consequence/action now say explicitly that this is the SmPC general gentamicin interaction text, that the systemic toxicities have not been reported after ear use and that systemic absorption after topical use is unlikely to give a comparable nephrotoxicity risk; note group:nephrotoxic now has members (ibuprofen, naproxen, methotrexate), so the gentamicin and neomycin/polymyxin/dexamethasone nephrotoxic rules are live for those oral products. Source conflicts that had been merged into one rule were split into separate rules (chloramphenicol pregnancy SmPC avoid + BUMPS info; chloramphenicol breastfeeding SmPC avoid + SPS caution; neomycin/polymyxin/dexamethasone pregnancy SmPC avoid + BUMPS info; breastfeeding SmPC caution + SPS info). The 4 ear no-uk-product decisions were confirmed (emc search: no results for the combinations).
